claim: Apple describes HealthKit's resting heart rate as an estimate of the lowest heart rate during rest.
quote: It is an estimation of  the user’s lowest heart rate during periods of rest, and is intended to be used as a medically relevant metric.

claim: Apple estimates it from sedentary heart rate samples taken through the day.
quote: the system estimates the resting heart rate by analyzing sedentary heart rate samples throughout the day.

claim: Apple may replace earlier resting heart rate samples with better estimates.
quote: the system may delete earlier samples and replace them with better estimates.

claim: Health Connect's resting heart rate record is one instantaneous measurement, with no derivation described.
quote: Each record represents a single instantaneous measurement.

claim: Google Health API's daily resting heart rate is calculated from all-day heart rate measurements.
quote: Measures the daily resting heart rate for a user, calculated using the all day heart rate measurements.

claim: Google Health API's calculation method can be with sleep data.
quote: The resting heart rate is calculated using the sleep data.

claim: Google Health API's calculation method can be awake data only.
quote: The resting heart rate is calculated using only awake data.

claim: Fitbit's Web API reference says the device uses heart rate through the day, favoring still, well-rested periods and sleep.
quote: To calculate resting heart rate, the device takes the heart rate measurements throughout the day and focuses on periods when the person is still and well-rested, with a priority for during sleep measurements.

claim: Fitbit returns no resting heart rate on a day without enough data.
quote: If there isn't enough data, a resting heart rate value won't be available for that day.

claim: Oura's sleep record reports the lowest heart rate during sleep.
Oura's readiness reports resting heart rate as a 1 to 100 contribution, not in beats per minute.
quote: Contribution of resting heart rate in range [1, 100].

claim: WHOOP's reference describes its resting heart rate field without saying how it is derived.
WHOOP's resting heart rate is one of the measurements behind the Recovery score.
quote: the Recovery object has objective measurements that factored into the score such as the resting heart rate (RHR), heart rate variability (HRV)

claim: Garmin's public Health API page lists heart rate among its metrics without a resting heart rate definition.
quote: Steps Intensity Minutes Sleep Calories Heart Rate Stress Pulse Ox Body Battery Body Composition Respiration Blood Pressure
